findings.title: website_name leaks the hidden website of TL0 users to anonymous viewers
findings.body:
`website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is hidden when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (TL0 users seen by anonymous). The new `website_name` attribute is derived from that same website but is not in that list, so it is always serialized.

Anonymous visitors therefore still get the TL0 user's website host and path. The template renders `model.website_name` in that case too, which defeats the anti-spam restriction.

The existing TL0 spec does not catch this because `untrusted_attributes` in the spec was not updated to include `website_name`. Fix: add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`.

findings.title: include_website_name missing `?`, so the filter is never invoked
findings.body:
ActiveModel::Serializers looks for `include_<attr>?` methods. This method is named `include_website_name` with no question mark, so it is dead code and `website_name` is never conditionally excluded.

It should be `include_website_name?`. Even then it would not apply the TL0 restriction unless it also checks `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` or the attribute is declared via `untrusted_attributes`.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic treats unrelated hosts under multi-part TLDs as the same domain
findings.body:
For hosts with the same number of labels (more than 2), the code drops only the first label and compares the rest. Examples where unrelated sites compare equal:
- `foo.co.uk` vs `forum.co.uk` (both reduce to `co.uk`)
- `alice.github.io` vs `forum.github.io` (both reduce to `github.io`)

In those cases an unrelated user site gets its full path displayed as if it were same-domain. A public-suffix-aware comparison would avoid this.

findings.title: `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal
findings.body: Using `<<` on a string literal mutates it in place. It works today, but it raises `FrozenError` once `frozen_string_literal` is enabled. Use interpolation (`".#{website_host}"`) or `+` instead.
